clue.text: An American Indian chief could make a long story longer

parts.note: a saga is a long story, originally a Norse epic
more can mean longer or further, as in 'a little more'

explanation.surface: A tribal leader is a fine subject for an endless, padded tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Longer' is a comparative standing in for MORE, not a definition of length.
explanation.definitionFit: A sagamore was a chief among Algonquian peoples of north-eastern North America.

clue.text: Staggers outside quietly and drives away

indicators.note: outside says the staggering word goes round the quiet letter

parts.note: staggers means reels, as a drunk does
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A tottering figure quietly forces off unwanted visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel an attacker is to drive them back or away.

clue.text: Blocking promotion

definitions.meaning: stopping up a hole, as with a stopper
advertising something persistently, as in pushing a new book

explanation.definitionFit: To plug is both to stop up a hole and to publicise a product repeatedly.

clue.text: Talk of an Irishman — soft rascal

parts.note: B marks a soft pencil lead (as in 2B)
a rogue is a rascal

explanation.surface: An Irishman's speech is that of a gentle scamp.
explanation.walkthrough: B for soft comes from pencil grading, where B leads are soft and H leads hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is the strong regional accent, especially Irish, in which someone speaks.

clue.text: Balance a vessel containing cold drink

indicators.note: containing tells us the ship holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a vessel
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
ale is a drink, beer

explanation.surface: A ship carries chilled beer in its hold, kept steady.
explanation.definitionFit: A balance is a weighing instrument, and so is a pair of scales.

clue.text: Mark, a good man, associated with rake surprisingly

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good man

indicators.note: surprisingly hints the letters of rake turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Mark is a decent chap, yet he is oddly linked with a libertine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name, with 'a good man' describing him; it is the definition, and the good man is a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: A streak is a long thin line or mark, such as a streak of paint.

clue.text: Pleased about a note, but certainly didn't look pleased

indicators.note: about says the pleased word goes round the musical note

parts.note: pleased means glad
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone happy about a message nevertheless scowled.
explanation.definitionFit: To glare is to stare angrily, the opposite of looking pleased.

clue.text: Note fish hang about

parts.note: D is a musical note
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: An angler leaves a message and waits about with his line.
explanation.definitionFit: To dangle is to hang loosely, swinging about.

clue.text: Hunter might well go ahead

parts.note: reads as a hunter pressing on, but means a hat with a peak at front and back, so either way is ahead; also a stalker of deer is a hunter

explanation.definitionFit: A deerstalker is both a hunter of deer and the cloth cap with peaks fore and aft.

clue.text: Get wrinkled serving men into condition

indicators.note: into says the soldiers go inside the condition word

parts.note: a case can be a condition, as in a bad case of flu
RE, the Royal Engineers, are serving soldiers

explanation.surface: Getting troops into shape leaves them crumpled.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps, so serving men.
explanation.definitionFit: To crease is to become wrinkled or folded.

clue.text: Attractive binding

definitions.meaning: committing or meshing together, as gears or a contract do

explanation.definitionFit: Engaging means charming, and also committing or interlocking, as gears engage.

clue.text: Interior decoration gives many trouble

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral 500, so many
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Doing up a room's interior causes endless bother.
explanation.walkthrough: A dado is the lower part of a room's wall, often panelled or papered differently.
explanation.definitionFit: A dado is a decorative band or panelling on the lower part of an inside wall.

clue.text: Schooled in cunning with much effort

indicators.note: in says the schooled word sits inside the cunning one

parts.note: sly means cunning
schooled means trained

explanation.surface: Someone taught to be crafty does it laboriously.
explanation.definitionFit: Done strainedly means forced, with visible effort and strain.

clue.text: Recent stage production of "The Spy"

indicators.note: a production makes something new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A new theatre staging of a play called The Spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production of' rearranges RECENT STAGE; the theatre picture hides the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A spy is an agent working in secret for a government.

clue.text: Prompter dealing with the baby-sitter?

parts.note: re means concerning or dealing with, as in letters
a minder looks after children, like a baby-sitter

explanation.surface: Someone who nudges about the baby-sitter's duties.
explanation.definitionFit: A reminder is something that prompts the memory, a prompter.

clue.text: Tells of an arrest being wrongly ordered

indicators.note: wrongly ordered says the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone recounts an unlawful arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to tell a story or recount events.

clue.text: A little crawler joining the currently popular party

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular now
a sect is a faction or party

explanation.surface: A creep sidling up to the fashionable faction.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect is a small creature that crawls, such as a beetle or ant.

clue.text: When overdue, a lot of books may be hidden

parts.note: late means overdue
NT is the New Testament, a collection of many books

explanation.surface: Overdue library books may be lurking somewhere out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Latent means present but hidden or not yet developed.

clue.text: Advise colleague in casual fashion

parts.note: to inform is to advise or tell
an ally is a colleague or partner

explanation.surface: Tipping off a workmate in a relaxed way.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally means in a casual, relaxed manner, without ceremony.

clue.text: Dreadful lout, a Western desperado

indicators.note: dreadful suggests these letters are in a terrible mess

explanation.surface: A nasty thug, a Wild West gunslinger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' rearranges LOUT and A into OUTLA, then W follows. 'a Western desperado' looks like one phrase, but Western gives only W.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlaw is a bandit beyond the law, a desperado.

clue.text: Cry out in pain, being chicken-hearted

parts.note: to yell is to cry out
ow is what someone in pain exclaims

explanation.surface: Someone screams in agony, showing their cowardice.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for cowardly, lacking courage.

clue.text: Some furniture — a desk etc — for study

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Items of furniture such as a desk are set out for a study room.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'etc — for study' is wrong: only 'study' defines READ, and 'etc — for' is link padding.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a subject, as at university, is to study it.

clue.text: A few words in condemnation

definitions.meaning: a grammatical unit of several words
the punishment passed by a court

explanation.definitionFit: A sentence is a group of words and also a judge's pronouncement of punishment.

clue.text: He going off, as the French say

parts.note: le is French for the
to aver is to say or declare

explanation.surface: A man departs, as the French would put it.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaver is someone who leaves or goes off.

clue.text: Darted about and arranged some deals

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A dealer rushed around striking bargains.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade is to buy and sell, making deals.

clue.text: An animal's lair amid rubbish

indicators.note: amid says the lair is placed in the middle of the rubbish

parts.note: rot means rubbish or nonsense
a den is an animal's lair

explanation.surface: A creature's home lies among the refuse.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodent, such as a rat, is a kind of animal.
